# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is an internal METR reference on how open AI labs turn experiments into final training
runs. Each lab chapter uses the same figures, built from `data/*.csv`, so the cross-lab chapter
can overlay them. The scope, lab tiers, and decisions are in the repository README.

## Data availability at a glance {.unnumbered}

What we would ideally have from every lab, against what each lab has actually published. Grades:
**●** published in a usable form, **◐** partial (stated for some releases, derived from stated
numbers, or figure-only), **○** not published. Evidence and sources are in `data/notes/*.md` and
the lab chapters. "Multiple generations" asks whether successive releases from the same lab let
recipe improvement be measured; "attribution" asks whether per-stage scores and per-stage
compute both exist for one model.

::: {.availability .column-page}

| Lab | Total spend, incl. people | Pretraining scaling curves | Post-training / RL curves | Multiple generations | Broad capability benchmarks | Attribution: pre- vs post-training |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Marin** | ◐ FTEs and funders named; no dollars, no compute total | ● Delphi IsoFLOP grid with per-run data; MoE and LR laws; every run on public W&B | ○ SFT only | ● 8B, 32B, Snowball 67B-A2B, 535B-A23B | ◐ 19-task base suite; not on ECI | ◐ SFT compute separable; base and instruct scored on different suites |
| **Ai2 OLMo** | ◐ Audited GPU-hours, 82% development; no dollars or staff count | ● OLMo ladder with fitted laws; W&B logs and checkpoints for finals | ○ RLVR hours reported, no curve | ● OLMo 1, 2, 3, 3.1, Hybrid | ● Broad suite; ECI not checked | ● Scores and GPU-hours per stage for one model |
| **Meta Llama** | ◐ GPU-hours per release; whole-project hours for Llama 1 only | ◐ Llama 3 IsoFLOP ladder, figure-only | ○ Described, no curves or compute | ● Llama 1 to 4; base MMLU comparable 1 to 3 | ● Full suite; 3.1 405B on ECI | ◐ Base and instruct scores; no post-training compute |
| **DeepSeek** | ◐ Dollar cost of the V3 and R1 final runs; experiments excluded | ◐ IsoFLOP suite and laws for DeepSeek LLM only; loss law figure-only | ◐ R1 step curves, figure-only | ● Seven releases, LLM to V4 | ● Broad suite; V2, V3, R1 on ECI | ● Base vs chat scores; post-training hours for V3 and R1 |
| **Prime Intellect** | ◐ Funding rounds; no GPU-hours for any RL run | ◐ OpenDiLoCo ladder; no law | ◐ Richest RL ablations, with failures; figure-only, no law | ◐ Five releases on three different base models | ● AIME, GPQA, LiveCodeBench, HLE; ECI not checked | ◐ Base-vs-post deltas; RL compute derived; base from another lab |
| **EleutherAI Pythia** | ◐ A100-hours incl. the discarded suite; no dollars | ● 70M to 12B ladder, 154 checkpoints each, W&B; no lab fit | ○ None | ◐ v0 to v1 fix only | ◐ Small-model suite; no MMLU | ○ No post-training |
| **Cerebras-GPT** | ◐ FLOPs per model; no hours or dollars | ● Fitted law, validated on the 13B; no logs | ○ None | ○ Single release | ◐ Small-model suite; no MMLU | ○ No post-training |

: Data availability by lab. ECI is Epoch AI's Capabilities Index. {#tbl-availability tbl-colwidths="[11,16,18,13,13,14,15]"}

:::

Three things stand out. Nobody publishes total spend including people: the closest are OLMo's
audited GPU-hours and DeepSeek's dollar figures for two final runs, and both exclude experiments
and salaries. Post-training scaling curves barely exist in public; Prime Intellect's ablations and
DeepSeek R1's step curves are figure-only. Attribution of capability to pre- versus post-training
is cleanest where a lab reports both per-stage scores and per-stage compute for one model, which
today means OLMo and DeepSeek.

Evidence behind the grades, one line per lab (sources in the notes files):

- **Marin.** Team size stated (1 to 10 FTE), funders named (Google TRC, Huang Foundation); compute
  exists only as our 6ND estimates (6.1e23 for 8B, 1.2e24 for 32B). Delphi is an 81-run IsoFLOP
  grid with per-run losses released; MoE and learning-rate laws are given in closed form; every
  8B and 32B phase and discarded run is on public W&B. The 8B instruct model is SFT-only (5.3B
  tokens against 12.7T), and base and instruct are scored on different suites, so there is no
  clean post-training delta.
- **Ai2 OLMo.** Morrison et al. 2026 audit the Olmo 3 pipeline at 8.34M GPU-hours with 82 percent
  in development, broken down by stage; no dollars, staff count or salaries. The OLMo ladder (16
  runs) publishes a fitted law per task; Olmo Hybrid adds a 7-size, 3-architecture ladder; the
  ladder's own W&B project is private. Per-stage scores (base, SFT, DPO, RLVR) and per-stage
  GPU-hours exist for the same 32B model, the cleanest attribution in the table.
- **Meta Llama.** GPU-hours per release (39.3M H100-hours for Llama 3); only Llama 1 states a
  whole-project figure (about 6M A100-hours, roughly 70 percent outside the shipped runs). The
  Llama 3 IsoFLOP ladder spans 6e18 to 1e22 FLOPs with a fitted exponent of 0.53, but is
  figure-only with run counts never stated; Llama 4 has no report. Base and instruct scores exist
  for the same models; post-training compute is never reported.
- **DeepSeek.** V3's 2.788M H800-hours ($5.58M) and R1's 147K ($294K) are the most precise
  final-run costs anywhere, split by stage and explicitly excluding experiments; author counts run
  86 to 318. The DeepSeek LLM paper gives a hyperparameter law, an IsoFLOP suite of about 80 runs
  and fitted allocation exponents, but the loss law is figure-only, and later generations publish
  fixed-scale ablations only. R1's AIME-versus-GRPO-step curves are figures. Base and chat scores
  are reported every generation; V3.2 states post-training above 10 percent of pretraining cost.
- **Prime Intellect.** Funding rounds ($5.5M, $15M, $130M) and headcount snippets; no GPU-hours or
  cost for any RL run. The RL ablation record (async delay, difficulty filtering, clipping,
  collapse modes, with failures) is the richest here but figure-only, from private W&B, with no
  fitted law. Each release starts from a different base model (own 10B, QwQ-32B, GLM-4.5-Air),
  so recipe gains and pretraining spend are not attributable to the lab.
- **EleutherAI Pythia.** 272K A100-hours for the released suite and 544K including the discarded
  first version; training compute donated by Stability AI. The suite is a 70M to 12B ladder on
  identical data with 154 checkpoints per model and public W&B logs; the lab fits no law. No
  post-training.
- **Cerebras-GPT.** Training FLOPs per model (3.1e22 in total) but no accelerator-hours or dollars.
  Seven compute-optimal sizes with the lab's own fitted law, validated out of sample on the 13B,
  plus a muP arm; figures and model-card losses only, no logs. Single release, no post-training.

**Reading the figures.** Every chapter opens with a scaling curve: training compute on a log
x-axis, loss or a benchmark on the y-axis, experimental runs as dots, the released model(s) as
stars, and a power law fitted to the experiments only, extrapolated out to where the final run
landed. The gap between star and line is how well the lab's experiments predicted its big run.
The compute-split bar under it is the cheap number: what share of logged compute went to
experiments rather than the final run. It is always a lower bound, because failed and unlogged
runs are missing.

**Confidence flags.** Every number in the data carries `reported` (stated by the lab),
`derived` (computed from reported numbers, method in the row), or `guess` (read off a figure).
Chapters state the flag wherever a number changes a conclusion.
